biography.background: Born April 1, 1975, in Cumming (Forsyth County), Georgia. Former Republican who publicly rejected Trump's 2020 election fraud claims. Spoke at 2024 Democratic National Convention as a Republican, urging 'Dump Trump.' Formally left the Republican Party and joined the Democratic Party on August 5, 2025. Expelled by Georgia Republican Party executive committee unanimously on January 6, 2025. Announced Democratic gubernatorial candidacy September 16, 2025.
partySwitchTimeline: 2020: Openly rejected Trump's election fraud claims as sitting Republican Lt. Governor
January 6, 2025: Expelled from Georgia Republican Party by unanimous executive committee vote
August 5, 2025: Published AJC op-ed announcing formal switch to Democratic Party, citing faith ('love thy neighbor') as motivating principle
August 21, 2024: Spoke at Democratic National Convention in Chicago, still identified as Republican, said 'dump Trump'

statedPositions.quote: As governor, Geoff will fight for Georgia families in all 159 counties — bringing down the cost of childcare, healthcare, and housing while ensuring our state rejects extremism and embraces the values of fairness, opportunity, and love thy neighbor.
statedPositions.notes: Homepage tagline. Three explicit pillars: affordability crisis, healthcare crisis, Donald Trump crisis.

statedPositions.quote: Would expand Medicaid; proposes $1.7 billion 'jumpstart fund' using 10% of Georgia's $17B rainy day reserves to cover Medicaid expansion and childcare/housing affordability
statedPositions.notes: Specific dollar figure and mechanism stated publicly. Also confirmed at Savannah forum (Jan 2026) and multiple interviews.

statedPositions.quote: Would use jumpstart fund to help single parents afford childcare; better funding of CAPS (Childcare and Parent Services) and TANF programs
Lowering housing costs is one of three affordability pillars; jumpstart fund would also target housing
statedPositions.notes: General commitment; no specific zoning or supply-side mechanism stated in available sources.

statedPositions.quote: On day one as governor, he would sign an executive order clarifying doctors can practice medicine with pregnant women without fear of prosecution and introduce legislation repealing Georgia's six-week ban.
statedPositions.notes: Explicit day-one executive order commitment. Full legislative repeal also stated.

statedPositions.quote: Supports universal background checks, red flag laws, and safe firearm storage requirements
statedPositions.notes: Three specific policy mechanisms named. Stated these were changed from prior positions driven by political pressure.

republicanRecord.note: Duncan held office exclusively as a Republican from 2013-2023. His record in this period represents his PRIOR positions. He has publicly recanted multiple stances — see positionConflicts section.

keyBills.summary: Forbids individuals under age 21 from working as bar bouncers
keyBills.notes: Named after Michael Bremer who died outside a bar

keyBills.summary: Established graduated penalties for cargo theft based on value stolen (misdemeanor under $500 to felony over $25,000)

keyBills.bill: HB 919 / SB 258 — Rural Hospital Tax Credit
keyBills.role: Original House sponsor (HB 919); provisions incorporated into Senate version SB 258
keyBills.summary: 70% state income tax credit for contributions to approved rural hospital organizations; cap $2,500 individual / $5,000 joint. Brought $250M+ to Georgia's rural hospitals.
keyBills.notes: Market-based (tax credit) approach to rural healthcare funding, consistent with Republican framework. Not Medicaid expansion.

ltGovernorRecord.role: President of Georgia State Senate; constitutional officer

keyLegislativeActions.outcome: Passed June 2020 — restored a hate crimes law to Georgia for first time in 16 years
keyLegislativeActions.notes: Built bipartisan coalition. Credited as instrumental. Duncan unveiled his version in June 2020 after Ahmaud Arbery killing.

keyLegislativeActions.outcome: Passed; repealed Georgia's archaic citizen's arrest law

keyLegislativeActions.bill: LESS Crime Act (Law Enforcement Strategic Support)
keyLegislativeActions.outcome: Passed House 153-5 (March 2022); signed by Governor Kemp (May 2022)
keyLegislativeActions.summary: Dollar-for-dollar state tax credit for contributions to local police/sheriff foundations. Funds can be used for officer salary increases, hiring, training, equipment, and co-responder mental health programs.
keyLegislativeActions.notes: Pro-police funding mechanism using tax credits. Consistent with Republican 'back the blue' framing, though includes mental health co-responder component.

keyLegislativeActions.bill: Georgia Behavioral Health and Peace Officer Co-Responder Act (SB 403)
keyLegislativeActions.summary: Framework for law enforcement partnerships with mental health professionals; co-response teams dispatched to behavioral health emergencies. Officers can consider mental health professional input in divert-to-treatment decisions.
keyLegislativeActions.notes: Reform-oriented within Republican frame: not defunding, but acknowledges mental health dimension of policing.

keyLegislativeActions.outcome: Signed by Governor Kemp 2019; bans most abortions after approximately 6 weeks
keyLegislativeActions.notes: Duncan was photographed smiling broadly at signing ceremony. Quote (pre-election 2018): 'I, of course, will support legislation that protects unborn children with heartbeats — an easy decision for me.' NOW RECANTED — see positionConflicts.

keyLegislativeActions.role: Presided over Senate passage as Lt. Gov.
keyLegislativeActions.outcome: Passed April 2022; gradually reduces Georgia individual income tax rate from 5.75% to 4.99% over 7 years — described as 'largest income tax cut in state history'
keyLegislativeActions.notes: Duncan touted this as pro-business. Republican supply-side fiscal approach.

keyLegislativeActions.outcome: Georgia did not expand full Medicaid under ACA during Duncan's tenure. Georgia adopted limited 'Pathways' work-requirement Medicaid expansion instead.
keyLegislativeActions.notes: Duncan has stated he 'explored every route possible to improve the state's health care system without expanding Medicaid' and concludes 'The answer is, you can't do it.' NOW RECANTED — see positionConflicts.

keyLegislativeActions.summary: As Lt. Governor, called for Georgia to expand school choice to 'close the skills gap.' Wrote AJC op-ed supporting school choice expansion.
keyLegislativeActions.notes: Republican-era position. No explicit 2026 recantation found, but no prominent 2026 advocacy either.

keyLegislativeActions.role: NRA A-rated; NRA-endorsed for Lt. Governor 2018
keyLegislativeActions.summary: NRA endorsement 2018; Facebook post touting 'A rating from the NRA.' NRA-PVF called him 'a strong advocate for law-abiding gun owners' with 'unwavering support of Second Amendment freedoms.'

scorecards.notes: This was his Republican-era rating. He now explicitly opposes the NRA and supports universal background checks and red flag laws. No current 2026 NRA grade found — he is running as a Democrat.

LCV scores federal and state legislators. Duncan served at state level in Georgia. No LCV scorecard found for Georgia state legislative office. No available score for his Lt. Governor tenure. Climate positions not prominent in 2026 campaign materials found.

Georgia Republican Party State Executive Committee voted unanimously on January 6, 2025 to expel Duncan from the party and prohibit future participation. Directly tied to his support for Kamala Harris in 2024 elections.

endorsements.organization: No major Democratic organizational endorsements found as of February 2026
endorsements.notes: Duncan is competing in a 7-candidate Democratic primary. He is framing electability as his core argument. No DSCC, Emily's List, labor union, or national Democratic endorsements surfaced in research.

Opponent Keisha Bottoms criticized Duncan: 'Georgians want a Governor who has fought to expand Medicaid instead of eliminate it, who protects reproductive rights rather than stands 100 percent against them.' This signals his prior record is an active liability with the Democratic base.

interviews.outlet: Atlanta Journal-Constitution (AJC) — 'Politically Georgia' podcast / candidate forum

keyExchanges.quote: I'm the only Democrat in this race that can beat a Republican because I've got Democrats, independents and disgusted Republicans that will show up and vote for me.
keyExchanges.notes: Core electability argument. Repeated across multiple outlets.

keyExchanges.quote: Some folks will say 'Geoff, have you lost your mind?' My answer is: No, I found my heart.
keyExchanges.notes: Marietta Daily Journal Q&A. Describes switch as 'faith journey' — could not 'square up' faith with Republican politics.

keyExchanges.quote: I got the issue of abortion wrong... I was wrong to think a room full of legislators knew better than millions of women. After taking the time to listen to the heartfelt stories, the difficult medical situations, the personal situations, I believe women deserve the right to choose.
keyExchanges.notes: Direct recantation of prior support for Heartbeat Bill.

keyExchanges.quote: As a former Republican I explored every route possible to improve the state's health care system without expanding Medicaid. The answer is, you can't do it.
keyExchanges.notes: Explicit recantation of prior anti-expansion position.

keyExchanges.quote: I didn't get the gun issue right... if we just would have been with ninety percent of Americans and believed in universal background checks and red flag laws, we'd be in a better position. I was wrong to think the NRA had anybody's best interest in mind — they simply have their own and are a fear mongering organization that puts pressure on legislators.
keyExchanges.notes: Explicit NRA criticism. Specific support for universal background checks and red flag laws.

keyExchanges.notes: Statement at American Legion hall near Atlanta, in front of Democratic activists. Apologized for all things done as a Republican.

positionConflicts.conflict: As Lt. Governor (2019), Duncan stood smiling at the signing ceremony of Georgia's Heartbeat Bill banning abortions at approximately 6 weeks, and prior to election said it was 'an easy decision for me.' As 2026 Democratic gubernatorial candidate, he calls this position 'wrong,' says he believes women deserve the right to choose, and has committed to signing a day-one executive order protecting doctors and introducing legislation to repeal the six-week ban.
positionConflicts.priorPosition: 100% against abortion; supported Heartbeat Bill at signing
positionConflicts.currentPosition: Pro-choice; repeal six-week ban; protect doctors from prosecution
positionConflicts.credibilityNote: Shift is unambiguous and repeatedly stated. Opponents (notably Keisha Bottoms) have specifically called out this flip as evidence of opportunism.

positionConflicts.conflict: As Lt. Governor, actively opposed full Medicaid expansion under the ACA. Georgia instead adopted a limited 'Pathways' work-requirement Medicaid program. As 2026 Democratic candidate, he says full expansion is the only viable path and commits to expanding it from day one, funded via the $1.7B jumpstart fund.
positionConflicts.priorPosition: Opposed full Medicaid expansion; backed limited work-requirement Medicaid
positionConflicts.currentPosition: Expand full Medicaid; fund via rainy day reserves
positionConflicts.credibilityNote: Explicitly acknowledges prior position was wrong.

positionConflicts.conflict: In 2018, touted NRA 'A rating' on Facebook and received NRA endorsement for Lt. Governor. NRA-PVF called him 'a strong advocate for law-abiding gun owners' with 'unwavering support of Second Amendment freedoms.' As 2026 Democratic candidate, calls the NRA 'a fear mongering organization,' says he 'didn't get the gun issue right,' and supports universal background checks, red flag laws, and safe storage requirements.
positionConflicts.priorPosition: NRA A-rated; endorsed by NRA; strong Second Amendment advocacy
positionConflicts.currentPosition: Universal background checks; red flag laws; safe storage; opposes NRA
positionConflicts.credibilityNote: 180-degree reversal. Acknowledged directly as prior error driven by 'political pressure.'

positionConflicts.conflict: As Lt. Governor, presided over passage of Georgia's 'largest income tax cut in state history' (HB 1437, 2022) — reducing top individual rate from 5.75% to 4.99%. As 2026 Democratic candidate, proposes spending $1.7B from rainy day fund on social programs. Fiscal philosophy appears to have shifted but no explicit recantation of the tax cut was found.
positionConflicts.priorPosition: Championed large income tax cut; supply-side fiscal conservatism
positionConflicts.currentPosition: Proposes jumpstart fund ($1.7B public investment for social services); no explicit tax position stated for 2026
positionConflicts.credibilityNote: No explicit recantation of tax cuts found. Gap in 2026 platform on tax policy.

positionConflicts.conflict: As Lt. Governor (2019-2020), wrote AJC op-ed advocating expansion of school choice to 'close skills gap.' As 2026 Democratic candidate, school choice has not been promoted or recanted in available sources.
positionConflicts.priorPosition: Supported school choice expansion as Republican Lt. Governor
positionConflicts.currentPosition: No 2026 statement found on school choice — neither endorsement nor recantation
positionConflicts.credibilityNote: This is a gap — not a clear conflict yet. Could surface during primary.

evidenceSummary.keyResearchNote: Duncan's profile is uniquely complex because he has both a Republican legislative record (2013-2023) AND a Democratic campaign platform (2025-present). The scorer must treat stated 2026 positions as the primary signal where they exist, flag the prior Republican record as context, and treat the explicit recantations as credible reversals — noting they are being contested by Democratic primary opponents. Do not assume positions that have not been explicitly updated.
evidenceSummary.overallConfidence: high for healthcare, firearms, abortion; medium for economic/fiscal; low to none for climate, immigration, transit, housing mechanics
evidenceSummary.sourceQuality: Strong. Multiple independent outlets (AJC, 11 Alive, GPB, Georgia Recorder, ABC/AP newswire) cover the same positions consistently. Primary sources include direct quotes from formal campaign launch, multiple Q&A events, and a statewide candidate forum.
